lead.title: Leads
lead.docsIntro: An external website or landing page uses this endpoint to submit a new lead. Every request must include a <1>valid API key</1> — otherwise the request is <1>rejected outright</1>.
lead.docsRateLimit: Rate limit: up to <1>300 requests</1> per 15 minutes for each API key. A request sent without a key or with an invalid key is <1>rejected</1> before it even reaches the limit.
lead.docsApiKeyDesc: To submit leads from Instagram, a Telegram bot or other integrations, the following header <1>must</1> be added to every request. <1>Do not share</1> this key with anyone.
lead.docsApiKeyHeaderRequiredValue: Yes — a request without the key is rejected outright
lead.docsApiKeyHeaderOwnerValue: Each admin has their own single key
lead.docsApiKeyHeaderEffectValue: If the key is valid the request is accepted with a 300/15min limit; if it is invalid or missing the lead is rejected outright
lead.docsApiKeyStep1: On sign-in each admin gets their own random key, different from everyone else's (created automatically on the first request).
lead.docsApiKeyStep2: The external integration (for example an Instagram webhook server) sends this key in the `x-lead-api-key` header on every POST request.
lead.docsApiKeyStep3: The server looks the key up in the Admin collection: if found, the request is accepted and counted against the 300/15min limit (tracked per key).
lead.docsApiKeyStep4: If the key is invalid, outdated or not sent at all, the request is <1>rejected immediately</1> and no lead is created.
lead.docsApiKeySecurity: Warning: the key is <1>as secret as a password</1>. Keep it only in server-side (backend) integration code — never put it in a frontend, mobile app or public repository. If you suspect the key has leaked, replace it <1>immediately</1> with the "Regenerate key" button — the old one stops working at once.
lead.regenerateConfirm: The old key will stop working and every integration using it must be switched to the new key. Continue?
